questions.q: What does a file's inode store?
options: The file's size, owner, permissions, times, and where its data blocks are, but not its name
A backup copy of the file
questions.explain: The name lives in the folder, as a "name → inode number" entry. That is why one inode can have several names (hard links).

questions.q: Bazaar's server says "No space left on device", but df -h shows the disk 40% used. What should you check?
options: df -i: the file system may be out of inodes (too many small files)
questions.explain: Every file uses one inode. Millions of tiny files can use them all while most of the space is free. The error message is the same.

questions.q: You rm a 2 GB log file, but the free space doesn't change. Why?
options: rm is slow and needs an hour
A running program still has the file open; the inode and its blocks are freed only when it closes the file
The file was too big to delete
questions.explain: rm only removes a name. The program's file descriptor still points to the inode. Restart or signal the program, or truncate the file instead.

questions.q: Why is open("products.json", "w") dangerous for an important file?
options: It empties the file immediately; a crash while writing leaves it broken, and the old version is gone
questions.explain: In the lab, a crash during an unsafe save left broken JSON and no good version at all.

questions.q: What is the safe way to replace products.json?
options: Write a temp file in the same folder, flush and fsync it, then os.replace() it over the real name
Delete the old file first, then write the new one
Write the temp file in /tmp and copy it
questions.explain: The rename is atomic: readers see the whole old file or the whole new one. A crash before it leaves the old file untouched.

questions.q: product.json and same_product.json show the same inode number in ls -li. You delete product.json. What happens?
options: same_product.json still has the data; it is a hard link to the same inode
questions.explain: The link count drops from 2 to 1. The data is freed only when the last name (and every open descriptor) is gone. A symlink, by contrast, would break.

questions.q: The same relative path, orders/order_1042.json, opens different files in two runs of Bazaar. Why?
options: A relative path starts from the process's current working directory, which was different
questions.explain: Build paths from a known absolute place, like Path(__file__).parent, not from wherever the program was started.

questions.q: import product works on a developer's Mac but fails in the Linux container. The file is called Product.py. Why?
options: macOS ignores upper/lower case in file names by default; Linux doesn't
Python files must be in capitals on Linux
questions.explain: On Linux, Product.py and product.py are different files. Match names exactly, and test in Linux containers.
